bib.title: Teaching Machines to Read and Comprehend

question: Can news articles and their summary bullets be turned into a large supervised reading-comprehension dataset, and can attention-based neural readers learn to answer its questions?
hypothesis: Neural models should suit the task, and attention-based models should outperform pure LSTM models.
contributions: A method to build large document-query-answer cloze data from news summaries with entity anonymisation and permutation (CNN, Daily Mail corpora, ~1M items)
Symbolic baselines (frame-semantic, word distance) and three neural readers (Deep LSTM, Attentive, Impatient)

method.summary: Cloze questions are made from CNN and Daily Mail summary bullets by replacing one entity with a placeholder. Entities are replaced by coreference-resolved markers that are permuted each time a data point is loaded. Heuristic baselines and Deep LSTM, Attentive and Impatient Readers are trained and compared on answer accuracy.

datasets.name: CNN
datasets.split: by time: train from April 2007 (95 months), valid March 2015, test April 2015
datasets.preprocessing: Coreference system, entities replaced by abstract markers, markers permuted on every load; articles over 2000 tokens and queries whose answer entity is not in the context filtered out

datasets.name: Daily Mail
datasets.split: by time: train from June 2010 (56 months), valid March 2015, test April 2015

models.name: Deep LSTM Reader
models.architecture: deep LSTM with skip connections; document then query (or query then document) fed as one sequence, delimiter |||
models.layers: depth searched over [1,2,4]; Table 6 does not list it

models.name: Attentive Reader
models.architecture: separate bidirectional single-layer LSTMs for document and query, token-level attention

models.name: Impatient Reader
models.architecture: as Attentive Reader but re-reads the document at each query token

models.name: Uniform Reader
models.architecture: Attentive Reader with all attention weights m(t) equal

models.name: Maximum frequency / Exclusive frequency
models.architecture: heuristic: most frequent entity in context (exclusive: not in query)

models.name: Frame-semantic model
models.architecture: PropBank frame triples with six rules in precedence order, on the unanonymised corpus; tuned on validation

models.name: Word distance model
models.architecture: sum of distances from each query word to nearest aligned context word, max penalty per word m = 8 tuned on validation

training.objective: inferred: maximise p(a|d,q) = softmax(W(a) g(d,q)) over vocabulary (cross-entropy)
training.dropout: Table 6: 0.2 Uniform/Attentive CNN, 0.3 Impatient CNN, 0.2 Uniform DM, 0.1 Attentive DM, 0.1 Impatient DM

limits: Frame-semantic baseline is a simplification, with poor coverage; authors expect the word-distance model to do much worse on question-style data.
Many queries are ambiguous (geographic placeholders) and coreference errors split one person into two markers (Appendix C).
No human performance ceiling reported; no seeds or variance; a single number per cell.
Memory limited the Attentive Reader to a single layer.
Authors concede many queries needing complex inference and long-range reference are unanswered.
